steps.what: Show the assignments for the senior camera crew members.
Meet directors and senior camera crews to discuss filming sequences and picture composition.
Record the camera movements and the composition they determined.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the assignments already written for the senior camera crew. The audio technician meets the director and the crew to discuss filming sequences, camera movements, and picture composition, and to determine them. The technician writes only what was agreed. The assignment does not determine the sequence. A production with no assignment leaves the screen blank.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments were mailed, and the sequence agreed in the room was written up later from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: The assignment can be open in the meeting. Determining the sequence still happens in the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Picture composition is agreed by looking at the people in the room, not by reading the assignment.
tasks.human_edge: The technician is in the meeting and writes the sequence the room determined.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays a meeting. The note records camera movements and composition the room agreed, and nothing is determined by the assignment sheet.

reach.task: Discuss a scene and leave with the blocking that was agreed.
reach.learn: The call sheet is not the agreement.

evidence.claim: An assignment already written names who is on the crew. It does not determine the filming sequence or the composition.
The sequence note is written by the technician from the meeting. The assignment does not contain the camera movements.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The production id and the assignments if they are already written. The sequence is not drafted before the meeting. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the assignments from the document store before printing them again.
unknowns: Whether the director, rather than the technician, writes the agreed sequence.
research_questions: Is the meeting in the room or on a call, and who must be present?

already_counted.description: The meeting and the note of what was agreed stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Close sequence notes for productions that were cancelled.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still meets the director and the camera crew and still writes the sequence they determined. Only showing assignments already written is removed. A production with no assignment saves nothing of the meeting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the last inventory of audio and videotapes.
Maintain inventories by counting audio tapes, videotapes, and related supplies.
Write the new count of tapes and supplies.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the last inventory of audio and videotapes. The audio technician counts the tapes and the related supplies and writes the new count. The last count is not copied forward as the new count. A store with no previous inventory leaves the screen blank, and the technician counts anyway. The screen does not count the shelf.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last count was a spreadsheet, and a new count sometimes repeated it without a visit to the shelf.
tasks.enabler_now: The last inventory can be shown for comparison. The count itself is still a visit to the shelf.
tasks.still_hard: Tapes can be out on a job, so the shelf and the last count will not match for a good reason.
tasks.human_edge: The technician counts the shelf and writes the new number. The last inventory is not the count.
tasks.altitude: The count stays a physical check. The last inventory is visible for comparison and is never written forward as the new count.

reach.task: Count stock on the floor rather than copy the last sheet.
reach.learn: The last number is not the count.

evidence.claim: Showing the last inventory is a lookup of a count already made. It is not a new count of the shelf.
The new count is written by the technician after the shelf is counted. Copying the last number would invent the stock.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.
Fields: The store id and the last inventory if one exists. The last count is not reused as the new count. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the last inventory from the document store before exporting it again.
unknowns: How often the shelf is counted, and whether tapes out on jobs are included.
research_questions: Who may adjust a count for tapes that are out of the building?

already_counted.description: Counting the shelf and writing the new count stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Archive inventories older than the company keeps.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still counts the tapes and supplies and still writes the new count. Only showing the last inventory is removed. The last count is never copied forward, so a week with no previous inventory still takes the full count.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List pieces and approximate times already printed in the programme.
Obtain and preview musical performance programs prior to the event.
Note an order that does not become familiar from that preview.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store lists the pieces and the approximate times already printed in the musical programme. The audio technician obtains and previews the performance prior to the event, to become familiar with the order. An order that does not match what was heard is noted by the technician. The printed list is not the listening. A programme with no printed order leaves the screen blank.
tasks.previous_blocker: The order of pieces arrived as a scan, and the technician learned the timings by watching a rehearsal with no list.
tasks.enabler_now: A printed order can be listed. Becoming familiar with the music still means listening.
tasks.still_hard: Approximate times on a page are not the time a piece actually takes in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The technician listens to the programme and notes an order that does not match.
tasks.altitude: The preview stays as listening. The printed order is shown so the technician can hear whether the event follows it.

reach.task: Know the order of pieces before the downbeat.
reach.learn: A printed time is not having heard the piece.

evidence.claim: Listing pieces and times already printed is a copy of the programme page. It is not a preview of the music.
Noting an order that does not match is the technician's note after listening. The printed page cannot hear the event.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The programme id and the piece names and times only if they are already printed. Times are not estimated by the screen. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the programme from the document already received before typing the order again.
unknowns: Whether the programme arrives as text or only as a scan the company has not read.
research_questions: How early before the event is the programme available to preview?

already_counted.description: Previewing the music and noting a mismatch stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Drop piece lists for events that have passed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still obtains and previews the musical programme by listening. Only listing pieces and times already printed is removed. A programme that arrives with no readable order saves nothing, because the list stays blank.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the approved announcement text for this production.
Perform narration of productions or present announcements.
Stop when the text in hand is not the approved announcement.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the announcement text if it is already approved for the production. The audio technician performs the narration or presents the announcement in the technician's own voice. The technician stops if the text in hand is not that approved text. No voice is generated. A production with no approved text leaves the screen blank, and the technician does not invent the words.
tasks.previous_blocker: The approved words were a late printout, and a wrong version was read on air.
tasks.enabler_now: The approved text can be shown. Speaking it stays with the technician.
tasks.still_hard: Delivery, pace, and pronouncing a name on air stay with the person speaking.
tasks.human_edge: The technician speaks the announcement. The screen only shows text that was already approved.
tasks.altitude: Narration stays in the technician's voice. Nothing is spoken unless the text was already approved, and no generated voice is used.

reach.task: Speak only the line that was agreed.
reach.learn: A text on screen is not the performance.

evidence.claim: Showing announcement text that is already approved is a lookup. It does not perform the narration.
A generated voice is not used. The announcement is spoken by the technician, so there is no synthetic voice to mark.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The production id and the announcement text only if it is already approved. The words are not drafted here. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the approved text from the document store. Do not add a voice tool.
unknowns: Whether narration is done by this technician or by a presenter.
research_questions: Who approves the announcement text before it may be spoken?

already_counted.description: Speaking the announcement and stopping a wrong text stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Remove announcement texts for productions that have aired.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still speaks the narration or the announcement. Only showing text that is already approved is removed. A production with no approved text saves nothing, and no voice is generated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician still meets the director, still counts the stock, still listens to the programme, and still speaks the announcement. A printed order of pieces is not the listening.
reach: Actors discuss a scene with a director, and this job learns the meeting stays a meeting.
Musicians and singers know the order of pieces, and this job learns the preview is still listening.
skills_to_grow: Agree the filming sequence in the meeting, and write only what was agreed.
Count the tapes rather than copy the last inventory.
Speak the announcement. Do not play a generated voice.
role.ambitious_version: Meetings, stock counts, listening, and narration stay with the technician. Stored lists open only what is already written.
